meta.titre: Convenience Foods in the Kitchen: Types, Benefits, Drawbacks and Fast Food
meta.sous_theme: Convenience and fast foods: types, reasons for popularity, advantages and disadvantages

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: On a busy morning in Douala a mother pours hot water on instant porridge, a student buys fried chicken and chips at lunch, and a trader opens a tin of sardines for supper. All three use foods that someone else has prepared. Such foods save time and effort but they can cost more and may carry a lot of salt, fat or sugar. Examiners like this theme because every candidate can give advantages and disadvantages, but only careful candidates give the exact number of different points.

items: Food processing means changing raw foods into other forms, for example by canning, drying or freezing.
Too much fat, sugar and salt in the diet can harm health.
Vitamins can be lost when food is processed, stored for long or cooked.

sections.titre: Convenience foods and fast foods: types, advantages and disadvantages
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Definition
A convenience food is a food that the manufacturer has partly or fully prepared, so that little time, skill or fuel is needed in the home kitchen. Fast food is hot food that is cooked and served quickly, often to be eaten at once or taken away: fried chicken and chips, burgers, meat pies, doughnuts and roadside grilled fish with plantain.

| Type | Examples |
|---|---|
| Ready to eat | bread, biscuits, canned sardines |
| Ready to heat | canned beans, canned soup, ready meals |
| Partly prepared (ready to cook) | cake mixes, packet soups, instant noodles, frozen vegetables, stock cubes |
| Dried or instant | powdered milk, instant porridge, custard powder |

### Advantages and disadvantages
| Advantages | Disadvantages |
|---|---|
| Save time and fuel | Many cost more per portion than a meal cooked from fresh ingredients |
| Need little skill or equipment | May contain much salt, sugar, fat and additives |
| Long shelf life, easy to store | Some vitamins lost in processing |
| Available out of season | Less control over what goes into the food |
| Little waste and a similar quality each time | Packaging adds to rubbish; people may eat them too often and cook less |

### Why they have become popular
More people work away from home and have little time; many homes have refrigerators, freezers and microwave ovens; towns have grown and supermarkets sell a wide variety; advertising promotes them; more people live alone or in small households.

### Fast food
It is quick, needs no cooking at home, is tasty and easy to buy. But it is often high in fat and salt and low in fibre and vitamins, regular use is costly, and hygiene may be poor where food is handled carelessly.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for a number of advantages and a number of disadvantages.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write two labelled lists with exactly the numbers asked. Each point must be a separate idea, and a disadvantage must not simply contradict an advantage. One mark is normally given per point, so a short sentence is enough. A vague phrase such as 'it is not good for you' earns nothing: say what harm, for example 'it is high in fat and salt'.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how a family can reduce the disadvantages of convenience foods.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Read the label for ingredients, salt, sugar and the expiry date; compare the cost of one portion with a home-cooked meal; add fresh vegetables or fruit to a packet meal; use convenience foods for busy days and not for every meal; throw away packaging properly.

sections.enonce_markdown: A family of 5 eats a fast-food meal that costs 1\,800 FCFA per person. The same meal cooked at home would cost 4\,500 FCFA for the whole family (assumed prices). (a) Calculate the cost of the fast-food meal for the family. (b) Find how much the family saves by cooking at home, as an amount and as a percentage. (c) Give two reasons other than money why a family may still choose fast food, and two health reasons for cooking at home. (8 marks)

etapes.action: Find the cost of the fast-food meal.
etapes.justification: Each of the five people pays the same price, so multiply.
Subtract the home-cooked cost from the fast-food cost.
Percentage saving is the saving divided by the original cost, multiplied by 100.

etapes.action: Give two non-money reasons for fast food.
etapes.justification: These are the advantages that attract busy families.
etapes.resultat_markdown: It saves time and effort; no cooking, washing up or fuel is needed.

etapes.action: Give two health reasons for cooking at home.
etapes.justification: At home the cook controls the ingredients.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Less fat and salt can be used, and fresh vegetables can be added.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **(a)** 9,000 FCFA. **(b)** The family saves **4,500 FCFA, which is 50 per cent**. **(c)** Fast food saves time and needs no cooking or fuel. Home cooking lets the family limit fat and salt and include fresh vegetables and fruit.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing 'convenience foods are cheaper' as an advantage.
items.pourquoi_faux: Many convenience foods cost more per portion than a meal cooked from raw ingredients. The true advantage is the time and fuel saved.
items.correction_markdown: Write 'saves time and fuel' and, if cost is mentioned, compare the price per portion.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving 'saves time' and 'quick to prepare' as two separate advantages.
items.pourquoi_faux: They are one idea in different words and earn one mark.
items.correction_markdown: Use a different idea for the second point, such as long shelf life or little skill needed.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that convenience foods contain no nutrients.
items.pourquoi_faux: Many give energy, protein and minerals. The real problems are that some vitamins are lost and that they may contain too much salt, sugar and fat.
items.correction_markdown: State the actual problem, for example 'some vitamins are lost in processing and salt and fat may be high'.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing 'it is not good for health' as a disadvantage.
items.pourquoi_faux: The statement is too vague to be credited.
items.correction_markdown: Say why: 'fast food is high in fat and salt and low in fibre, which can lead to obesity and heart disease'.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Define the term convenience food. (b) Name two dried convenience foods. (c) State two advantages of using canned foods.
items.solution_markdown: (a) A food that has been partly or fully prepared by the manufacturer so that little time or skill is needed at home. (b) Any two, for example **powdered milk, instant porridge, custard powder**. (c) Any two: long shelf life; ready to eat or heat quickly; saves time and fuel; can be stored without a refrigerator until opened.

items.enonce_markdown: A family of 6 buys fast-food meals at 1\,500 FCFA per person on 4 days in one week. Cooking the same meals at home costs 5\,400 FCFA per day for the family (assumed prices). (a) Calculate the cost of the fast food for one day and for the week. (b) Calculate the cost of home cooking for the 4 days. (c) Find the saving and express it as a percentage of the fast-food cost. (d) State one reason why the family may still prefer fast food.
items.solution_markdown: (a) One day: $6 \times 1\,500 = 9\,000$ FCFA. Week: $9\,000 \times 4 = 36\,000$, so **36,000 FCFA**. (b) $5\,400 \times 4 = 21\,600$, so **21,600 FCFA**. (c) $36\,000 - 21\,600 = 14\,400$ FCFA saved. $\dfrac{14\,400}{36\,000} \times 100 = 40$, so **40 per cent**. (d) It saves time and effort because nobody has to cook or wash up.

items.enonce_markdown: Discuss the statement: 'Fast food is a poor choice for a growing teenager.' (8 marks)
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for a balanced answer. **For the statement (about 4 marks):** fast food is often high in fat, salt and sugar; it may be low in fibre, vitamins and calcium that growing bones need; regular eating can cause overweight and heart disease later; it can replace more balanced family meals; hygiene may be poor. **Against the statement (about 3 marks):** it supplies energy and some protein; it is quick when a teenager has little time; an occasional fast-food meal does no harm if the rest of the diet is balanced. **Conclusion (1 mark):** fast food is acceptable now and then but a teenager needs mostly balanced meals with vegetables, fruit and milk products.

items_markdown: A convenience food is partly or fully prepared by the manufacturer; fast food is hot food cooked and served quickly.
Advantages: saves time, fuel and skill; long shelf life; available out of season. Disadvantages: many cost more per portion; may be high in salt, fat and sugar; some vitamins lost.
Popularity is due to busy working families, refrigerators and microwaves, supermarkets, advertising and small households.
In 'state' questions, write exactly the number asked and make every point a different idea; never use a vague phrase such as 'unhealthy'.
Compare the cost of one portion before saying that a convenience food is cheaper or dearer than home cooking.
